public_rationale: The contract reads the claim as: as of the post date (August 25, 2025), AI could not reliably do software development on its own, so coding could not simply be handed to it. It does not read it as: AI cannot write any code. METR's independent evaluation of GPT-5 was published August 7, 2025. It estimated a 50% chance of success on software tasks that take a professional about 2 hours 17 minutes (95% CI 65 minutes to 4 hours 25 minutes) (e1, e2). It put the 80% time horizon at about 25 minutes (95% CI 8 to 65 minutes), compared with 20 minutes for OpenAI o3 and Claude Opus 4 (e2). These results show useful coding capability. They also show frequent failures on software tasks of modest length, which meets the contract's support condition. The packet contains no evidence from that period of AI reliably completing software development end to end without human coding expertise.
limitations: The claim states no threshold for reliability or task size, so the result depends on the plain reading of 'just handle coding'.
The evidence comes from one evaluator's task suite. Its tasks differ from full product development.
The search was not exhaustive for individual cases of non-coders building working software with AI.
This assessment covers only the period just before the post (July 1 to August 25, 2025).

He describes the current state without naming a period. I use the period just before the post (July 1 to August 25, 2025), when the latest frontier models had been released and independently measured.
Independent measurements of how reliably frontier AI agents complete realistic software-engineering tasks on their own are fair evidence.
criteria.support_condition: Independent evaluations from around the post date show that frontier AI agents fail often on realistic software tasks of modest length, so they cannot be relied on to handle coding on their own.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence from around the post date shows AI systems reliably completing realistic software development work end to end, without human coding expertise, at a level where coding could be handed off to them.
